name: Screaming Trees
label: SST
lede: Two brawling brothers rehearsed in their parents' video store in Ellensburg, Washington, with a singer whose voice sounded like a burnt church. Seattle's boom put them on Epic and Letterman, and the band still ended without a goodbye.

eras.title: Rehearsals in the family video store
eras.text: Ellensburg, Washington, sits 107 miles east of Seattle, and in the mid-'80s it had nowhere for a band like this to play. Two brothers, a drummer and a former high school quarterback made records anyway, on their parents' money.

years.big: "My mom told them they had to have me in the band."
years.h: Mark Lanegan's first rehearsal is in Gary Lee Conner's bedroom
years.p: [[Van Conner|11822f2b-d2e1-41dc-9879-a814d6a9dfea]] and drummer [[Mark Pickerel|90fd60fc-b149-4d97-a4fc-54b8b767ad42]] invite Lanegan to rehearse in Van's brother Gary Lee's bedroom. [[Gary Lee Conner|a89062ce-a507-49b7-a5d0-6dc67f99e4a5]] tells Kerrang his own seat in the band came courtesy of his mother.
years.xp:
Lanegan had been a high school quarterback. The Conner brothers had found punk through Black Flag's Damaged in 1981. Gary Lee dates it to the summer of 1985: "me, my brother Van and Mark Pickerel were doing a weird combo."

The band practiced in the Conner family's video rental store, where members also worked. They took their name from an Electro-Harmonix guitar effects pedal, the Screaming Tree.

years.h: Screaming Trees cut the Other Worlds demo in Ellensburg
years.p: Producer [[Steve Fisk|c851ef86-5278-4537-8b51-7ccedb4ae903]] works at Creative Fire. K Records distributes the tape first, then Ellensburg's Velvetone. Gary Lee Conner says the band couldn't even get a gig in town.

years.h: The Conner parents pay for Clairvoyance
years.p: The band's first full-length, on Velvetone, mixes psychedelia and hard rock. Louder says it sold 2,500 copies, impressive for a band from the backwaters of the Pacific Northwest.

eras.title: A tape for Greg Ginn
eras.text: A demo handed to Greg Ginn at a Black Flag show got an Ellensburg garage band onto SST, the label its members worshipped. Three albums in three years followed, made between months in a van and fistfights between brothers.

years.h: [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]] gets a tape in Olympia, and SST signs Screaming Trees
years.p: The tape goes to Ginn after a Black Flag show; he offers a contract, and the debut is Even If and Especially When. Gary Lee Conner calls the signing "a total dream come true for everybody."
years.xp: The band handed Ginn the tape after seeing Black Flag in Olympia. Life on SST meant months in a van, a show every night and sleeping on strangers' floors, then going home to save money for the next run.

years.h: Invisible Lantern follows on SST
years.p: Album two for the label brings more of the Conner brothers' psychedelic garage rock.

years.h: Producer Jack Endino watches the Conner brothers wrestle on the studio floor
years.p: The rest of the band tells him they do it all the time. Buzz Factory is the last Screaming Trees album for SST.
years.xp: Wikipedia says difficulties with the label led the band to leave. Next stop was Sub Pop, with the Change Has Come EP.

years.h: Lanegan, Kurt Cobain and Krist Novoselic record as the Jury
years.p: Pickerel joins them, and they cut Lead Belly songs under that name.

years.h: A van wreck in Florida leaves Lanegan wondering whether to go on
years.p: Gary Lee Conner says that after the late 1989 crash on the Buzz Factory tour, Lanegan wondered out loud whether he wanted to keep going.
years.xp: Conner told Kerrang the crash "wasn't serious, luckily, but we were held up for a couple of days."

years.h: Sub Pop releases the Change Has Come EP
years.p: Steve Fisk produces half and Jack Endino the other half. Pickerel called it the band's best recorded moment.

eras.title: Seattle goes major, and Screaming Trees go with it
eras.text: Seattle's big bang pulled Screaming Trees onto a major label, into Soundgarden's orbit and onto a soundtrack everyone owned. It also put the band's drinking and its fights on national television.

years.h: Lanegan goes solo, and Cobain turns up on The Winding Sheet
years.p: Sub Pop releases it. Cobain and Novoselic appear on Lead Belly's Where Did You Sleep Last Night.

years.h: Chris Cornell co-produces the Epic debut, Uncle Anesthesia
years.p: Terry Date and Soundgarden's [[Chris Cornell|cbf9738d-8f81-4a92-bc64-ede09341652d]] produce, and Cornell's wife Susan Silver manages the band. Bed of Roses reaches No. 23 on the Modern Rock chart.

years.h: Drummer swap: Pickerel leaves, [[Barrett Martin|2faf3b65-f4fa-4465-b0b7-c06370f0a63e]] arrives
years.p: Screaming Trees' original drummer goes; Martin replaces him. Pickerel forms the band Truly the same year.

years.h: The crew van rolls over on black ice in Wyoming
years.p: It's a serious rollover on the road to Sweet Oblivion. Gary Lee Conner says it actually brought the band closer.

years.h: Cameron Crowe puts Nearly Lost You in Singles
years.p: The Seattle movie sets Screaming Trees beside Pearl Jam and Soundgarden. The song reaches No. 5 on Modern Rock and No. 50 in the UK.

years.h: Cobain invites Screaming Trees to Nirvana's Reading day
years.p: Screaming Trees play the last day of the 1992 Reading Festival, with [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] headlining, at Cobain's invitation. They play Roskilde with Nirvana that year too.

years.h: Sweet Oblivion becomes the breakthrough
years.p: Wikipedia puts U.S. sales at 300,000. Dollar Bill follows Nearly Lost You onto the Modern Rock chart.
years.xp: Martin described a fine balance in the band between being creative and destructive. Louder reports Lanegan was fighting heroin addiction at the same time.

yt: Nearly Lost You on Letterman, October 16, 1992
years.h: Lanegan sings on Letterman with a black eye from a bar fight
years.p: The night before, Screaming Trees fight locals at a New Jersey bar. Lanegan performs Nearly Lost You on Late Night with the black eye, and Martin is hurt.
years.xp: Revolver says Martin broke his arm and couldn't play the next night. Louder says he dislocated his shoulder and puts the bar in Asbury Park.

years.big: "They threatened not to support our records if we didn't do it; they acted like gangsters."
years.h: Epic tells Screaming Trees to open for [[Alice in Chains|4bd95eea-b9f6-4d70-a36c-cfea77431553]]
years.p: Barrett Martin says that instead of headlining bigger rooms, the band had to take the Alice in Chains tour or lose label support.
years.xp: In summer 1993 they were sent out opening for the Spin Doctors. Martin told Louder: "Us and the Spin Doctors. Playing support is not how to make a career out of a band." Louder also reports shows cancelled because of the band's drinking.

eras.title: Grunge's nearly men
eras.text: By the time Dust arrived in 1996, most of their Seattle peers had broken big or broken up. Screaming Trees added a young Josh Homme, played Lollapalooza and kept brawling.

years.h: Van Conner takes a break to play bass for [[Dinosaur Jr.|77c167d2-4965-4421-830a-9815e4956475]]
years.p: After the Sweet Oblivion tour, Van leaves for a while to back [[J Mascis|82315599-2215-4c3e-a36f-87be58d06ec0]]. [[Donna Dresch|a192432c-67e4-4eef-af43-25c6fb901a7b]] fills in at Screaming Trees shows.
years.xp: The band also had a habit of throwing beer cans at each other. Barrett Martin tells Loudwire of one hurled in Lanegan's New York hotel room that set off a brawl between the Conner brothers and ended with a vintage refrigerator falling on him.

yt: All I Know, Later with Jools Holland, 1996
years.h: Dust arrives nearly four years after Sweet Oblivion
years.p: Made with George Drakoulias, it reaches No. 134 on the Billboard 200. All I Know hits No. 9 on the Modern and Mainstream Rock charts, and Newsday calls them grunge's most accomplished band.

years.h: Josh Homme joins on second guitar
years.p: The ex-[[Kyuss|ea0f2a37-7007-4217-a812-396227f5013a]] guitarist tours with Screaming Trees until 1998.
years.xp: Gary Lee Conner told Kerrang: "Having him there freed me up, and that was when I did some my best playing."

years.h: Lollapalooza puts Screaming Trees on a bill with the Ramones and Metallica
years.p: Van Conner calls sharing a bill with the [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] a childhood dream come true.

years.h: Lanegan is arrested for crack possession mid-tour
years.p: Louder reports he spent the next eight months in rehab in Joshua Tree. Martin says it was better to miss a tour and have everyone survive.

eras.title: No label, no goodbye
eras.text: The last Screaming Trees album was finished and nobody wanted it. The band played one final show at a Seattle museum opening and, by Gary Lee Conner's account, never told him it was over.

years.h: The last album gets made at Studio Litho
years.p: [[Stone Gossard|ca7e6e03-4973-45ef-8833-98774a2d4138]]'s studio hosts the sessions while Lanegan is also busy with his solo album Scraps at Midnight. The 1999 demos, including Ash Grey Sunday, find no label.
years.xp: Louder dates the Studio Litho sessions to winter 1998.

years.h: The last show is a museum opening, and one guitarist doesn't know
years.p: Screaming Trees play the opening of Seattle's Experience Music Project, then announce their breakup. Gary Lee Conner says nobody told him it was over.
years.xp: Conner told Kerrang: "I didn't know until after the last show when someone mentioned it in the dressing room."

eras.title: Last words, and a feud in print
eras.text: Mark Lanegan joined Queens of the Stone Age and kept his solo career going. The band's lost album came out 11 years after the breakup, his memoir reopened old wounds, and within a year of each other Lanegan and Van Conner died.

years.h: Queens of the Stone Age bring in Lanegan as one of three singers
years.p: Josh Homme's band gives him a seat; he makes two albums with them before leaving in late 2005. His solo record Field Songs comes out in May.

years.cap: Mark Lanegan at Bumbershoot, Seattle, September 2009
years.h: Eleven years late, Last Words
years.p: The 1998-99 recordings, mixed by Jack Endino and Martin, finally come out digitally on Sunyata.

years.h: Gary Lee Conner answers Lanegan's memoir
years.p: Posting on Facebook, Conner says he read only a few pages of Sing Backwards and Weep, in which Lanegan takes aim at his old bandmates.
years.xp: Conner wrote that the book is "delivered with a venom that is perplexing," and that he had moved past the old conflicts years ago. He also said he's proud of what the band made together.

years.h: Mark Lanegan dies at home in Killarney at 57
years.p: Mark Lanegan, sober for about two decades, died at his home in County Kerry, Ireland. The Irish Times reports a coroner found misadventure: a fall he couldn't survive, weakened by long COVID.
years.xp: In March 2021 Lanegan spent close to a month in a coma with COVID at University Hospital Kerry. According to his nephew in the Irish Times, his lungs never fully recovered.

years.h: Van Conner dies at 55
years.p: Van Conner had been in a coma after stomach surgery, then caught COVID-19. Wikipedia says pneumonia caused his death.
